intro.h2: A design studio that also runs the build
paragraphs: OKC Kitchen & Bath offers kitchen remodeling in Oklahoma City for homeowners who want design and construction under one roof. The team works from an office in Midtown at 12 NW 13th St., and projects reach across the metro, including Edmond and Nichols Hills. Full interior design is part of every job, not an add-on.

The firm is upfront about fit: projects include full interior design services and begin at $40,000. That lets the team spend real time on each home, from mood boards to a cabinet meeting held in your own kitchen. Reviewers name the crew members and say communication stayed clear from the first call to the last day.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Oklahoma City, plus baths and whole homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodel
items.blurb: Layout, lighting, custom cabinetry and finishes planned together, so the kitchen works as well as it looks. A cabinet meeting at your home settles sizing, spacing and storage before construction. One client went from a 1980s kitchen to a modern one, gold sink included.

image.alt: Evergreen kitchen remodel with muted green cabinets, a white quartz island and stainless steel appliances

items.name: Bathroom Remodel
items.blurb: Bathrooms built for calm, using timeless materials and bespoke details. Past work runs from a moody black-tile bath to a primary bath with a soaking tub and a 10-foot floating vanity. Showers, vanities, tile and lighting are designed and installed by the same team.

image.alt: Stone Gate Lodge bathroom with green handmade tile walls, a long dark-topped double vanity and a glass shower enclosure

items.name: Whole Home Renovation
items.blurb: Several rooms remodeled with one consistent design. The Stone Gate Lodge combined an expanded kitchen, an opened-up bath, refinished hickory, iron railings and a pair of new iron doors, with soapstone and unlacquered brass chosen to patina over time.

image.alt: Renovated staircase with wood treads, black iron railings and white walls in the Stone Gate Lodge whole-home remodel

items.name: Interior Design
items.blurb: Design is in-house and included in every project. Senior Designer Mel Wanzer leads in-person design meetings, builds mood boards with curated material options and helps you choose finishes. Reviewers say the team had great ideas about color and design, and one found the exact gold sink a client wanted.

about.text: OKC Kitchen & Bath is owned by Ryan Johnson, Owner and Head of Construction, and Cynjn Johnson, Owner and Head of Pre-Construction. Together they run a design-build team in Midtown Oklahoma City that treats each home as a living work of art. Senior Designer Mel Wanzer leads design and selections, and Director of Field Operations Chandler Francis runs the work in the field. The company follows five core values, including Right Things, Right Way and Present in the Work. One Edmond client wrote that Cynjn did everything he promised.

process.h2: Seven steps, from discovery call to final walkthrough

steps.title: Discovery call
steps.text: A phone call about your goals and budget to make sure OKC Kitchen & Bath is the right partner before anyone visits.

steps.title: In-home consultation and proposal
steps.text: The team walks your space, then you meet at the Midtown office to review a proposal and an early visual direction.

steps.title: Design and selections
steps.text: In-person design meetings and mood boards with curated materials, refined with you until every element fits your vision.

steps.title: Cabinet meeting
steps.text: A meeting in your home about cabinet sizing, spacing and function, so storage and daily flow work before the build begins.

steps.title: Build and walkthrough
steps.text: Construction follows the agreed plan with clear communication, and ends with a detailed cleaning and a final walkthrough together.

service_area.h2: Serving Oklahoma City, Edmond, Nichols Hills and Norman
service_area.text: The team completes full-service projects across the Oklahoma City metro from its Midtown office. The site names Oklahoma City, Edmond and Nichols Hills, and past clients quoted on the home page live in Newcastle, Edmond and Norman. Proposal meetings happen at the Midtown office and design meetings are held in person, so most work stays within driving range of downtown.

faq.h2: Before you book a discovery call

items.q: What is the minimum project size?
items.a: Projects include full interior design services and begin at $40,000. The contact form asks you to pick a budget range, from $40,000 to $60,000 up to $200,000 and more, and a start window of as soon as possible, three to six months, or six months or later. That helps the team prepare for your call.

Design is included. OKC Kitchen & Bath works as a design-build firm with an in-house designer, so you meet in person to review inspiration, build mood boards and pick materials. The same company then builds what you approved, which keeps the plan and the construction lined up.

It is step five of the process. Before construction begins, the team meets at your home to review cabinet sizing, spacing and function. The goal is a layout that works for daily life, from where appliances sit to how storage and traffic move through the room.

items.q: Can you keep some of my existing features?
items.a: Often, yes. One Norman client asked to keep the original cabinets in both her kitchen and master bathroom, and the team worked them into the final design while replacing the flooring through most of the house. Mention anything you want to keep on your discovery call.

The discovery call is by phone. The team then visits your home for a consultation and invites you to the Midtown Oklahoma City office at 12 NW 13th St., Suite 1E, to review the proposal and an early visual direction with the in-house designer.

final_cta.text: Call (405) 693-4737 or send your project details online, and the team will set up a call about your goals, timing and budget.
